labels.reason: Not caused by #1810: the full-date overlap check (season_validators.validate) predates it; #1810 only routed season writes through templates.load_owned/save, and the blamed load_owned lines are where #2107 adds next-occurrence dating; the bug itself is date semantics (full date vs month/day), not a key or inheritance link.

Not caused by #1367, which only moved report_service.py with git mv; the only blamed line is its lint-baseline entry, and the swallowed AttributeError on a missing drop_off/pick_up predates the move (an optional-attribute/None bug, not a data key).

#1866 wrote the is_valid test in _add_trace_ids, but the breakage is a span-state condition (valid vs sampled) that surfaced when ansible#484 turned on 1-in-10 sampling; nothing travelled through a data key or inheritance link.
Not caused by #1386, which only moved season_pricing.py; the blamed line is its lint-baseline entry, and the None-date AttributeError in is_day_in_season predates the move.

Not caused by #1120: its users early-return in the photo-count check was correct and was only rewritten; the repaired bugs (photos attached only by the async images:update:entity job, lost updates on picture, cap counted against stored photos) predate it.

Not caused by #1664: the review endpoint's 403-vs-404 difference already existed (the PR's own comment says so) and #1664 only attached error codes to the existing raises; an error code is a response value, not a data key.

Not caused by #1194: its own exclude (ownima-backend/app/tests/fixtures/release_please/.*) was already anchored from the repository root and correct; #2006 fixed the other ^app/ patterns and only rewrote #1194's comment and line in passing; a pre-commit path regex is not a data key.
Not caused by #1375 (a test-only style cleanup); the only blamed line is fake_opensearch.py's lint-baseline count, and the fake returning empty hits for match_phrase/ids/wildcard predates it.

#1893's priming of status="5xx" was correct when it merged; #1920 itself switched the instrumentator to ungrouped status codes and adapted the priming in the same PR, so the breaking PR did not cause a breakage.
Not caused by #1866: the worker never called setup_logging() before it either; #1866 only contributed a comment line in worker/base.py that #1892 touched.

Not caused by #1102: PIT exhaustion comes from opening a point-in-time per paginated search with a 10-minute keep_alive, which predates it; #1102 only added the scoped fallback and its logger.exception, which #1885 edited.
Not caused by #1866: shutdown never cancelled the queue-depth-monitor background task; #1866 only added shutdown_tracing() to the close chain that #1882 re-nested.
Not caused by #1631, which moved the painless rental-days script verbatim from analytics.py to queries.py; the millisecond-based average predates it and is a formula error, not a key break.

Not caused by #1633, which moved the prefix-on-_id clause verbatim from reservations.py into queries.reservation_list; the clause (refused by OpenSearch 3 on the _id field) predates it, as #1839 itself notes.

Not caused by #1810, which only renamed request.price_template to template around the existing zip(strict=False) and `or default` lines; the zero-price fall-through predates it and is a count/validation bug, not a key or inheritance link.
